system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — NewStar Financial, Inc. realized record after acquisition by First Eagle, ~3-5-year horizon (~2020-2022)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The acquired entity terminated its SEC
> registration shortly after closing and has filed no periodic report since; the
> realized-record facts below are limited to what is traceable through EDGAR's public
> filing history for the entity's CIK. This sub-dossier contains no information about
> how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On January 2, 2018, NewStar Financial, Inc. filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination
  of registration of its common stock under Section 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act
  of 1934, stating an approximate number of holders of record of "1." [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-000376, Form 15-12B]
- No Form 10-K, 10-Q, 20-F, or other periodic report has been filed under CIK 0001373561
  since the Form 15-12B in January 2018, per the entity's public EDGAR filing history.
  [SRC: SEC EDGAR company filing history, CIK 0001373561, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001373561]
- Consequently, no audited public financial statements specific to the acquired business
  exist for the ~2020-2022 outcome window, and no periodic filing discloses a
  post-acquisition net income/loss, impairment, or comparable financial-performance
  scalar for this entity. [SRC: SEC EDGAR company filing history, CIK 0001373561]

## Later corporate record under the same CIK
- EDGAR's registrant-name history for CIK 0001373561 records the entity's name as
  "NewStar Financial, Inc." until September 11, 2018, and as "First Eagle Private
  Credit, LLC" thereafter. [SRC: SEC EDGAR submissions data, CIK 0001373561, https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001373561.json]
- Under the name "First Eagle Private Credit, LLC," the entity (together with roughly
  thirty affiliated First Eagle investment-management and fund entities, including
  "First Eagle Alternative Capital BDC, Inc." and "First Eagle Private Credit Advisors,
  LLC") was a co-applicant on a Form 40-APP application filed August 13, 2020 (amended
  through 2020) seeking an Investment Company Act exemptive order permitting certain
  joint transactions among the named funds. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-218989, Form 40-APP]
- That Form 40-APP is a regulatory application for co-investment exemptive relief across
  a fund complex; it does not report NewStar's/First Eagle Private Credit's own revenue,
  income, assets, or operating results, and is not a periodic financial disclosure of the
  acquired business. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-218989, Form 40-APP]
- "First Eagle Alternative Capital BDC, Inc." (CIK 0001464963), which files annual
  reports on Form 10-K, is a separate, independently registered business development
  company (formerly organized under a different name) that predates the NewStar
  transaction and is advised by a First Eagle affiliate; its 10-K reports that BDC's own
  investment portfolio and results, not a segment specific to the entity acquired from
  NewStar's stockholders in the 2017 merger. [SRC: SEC EDGAR company filing history, CIK 0001464963]

## Ultimate parent's public-disclosure posture
- First Eagle Investment Management, LLC, the ultimate parent of the acquiring entities,
  was described at the time of the transaction as an independent, privately-owned
  investment management firm. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-355921, DEFM14A "The Parties to the Transactions"]
- No SEC filing has been identified in which First Eagle Investment Management, LLC or
  an affiliate separately discloses the post-acquisition financial or operating
  trajectory of the business acquired from NewStar's stockholders. [UNVERIFIED — absence
  confirmed only to the extent of the EDGAR full-text and company-filing searches
  performed for this dossier; a private firm's non-public disclosures cannot be ruled out.]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The acquired entity terminated its SEC reporting obligations approximately eleven days
  after closing and has filed no subsequent periodic report; the entity's later EDGAR
  filing activity under the same CIK consists solely of a fund-complex exemptive-relief
  application (2018-2020) that names it among many affiliated entities but discloses no
  entity-specific financial or operating results. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-000376, Form 15-12B]; [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-218989, Form 40-APP]
- No public 3-5-year record of the acquired business's realized financial or operating
  trajectory is available; the ultimate parent is privately held and has not been found
  to separately disclose that business's results. [SRC: SEC EDGAR company filing history, CIK 0001373561]; [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-355921, DEFM14A "The Parties to the Transactions"]

[SLICE END]
